From the eigenvalue classification we obtain the expressions for the matrix entries \(U(t)_{0,d}\). The requirement that all amplitudes to vertices other than \(0\) and the antipode \(p\) vanish forces \(\sin\!\big(\tfrac{p t}{2}\big)=0\), i.e. \(t=\tfrac{2\pi m}{p}\) with \(m\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).  

At such times the amplitudes reduce to  
\[
U(t)e_{0}= \cos t\,e_{0}+ i\sin t\,e_{p},
\]
so a genuine fractional revival occurs provided \(\sin t\neq0\). The smallest positive integer \(m\) that satisfies this while keeping \(\sin t\neq0\) is \(m=1\), giving the minimal revival time  
\[
t^{*}= \frac{2\pi}{p}.
\]

The derivation matches known special cases (e.g., \(p=3\) yields the well‑known fractional revival on the 6‑cycle) and there are no hidden steps or missing eigenvalue contributions. Thus the closed‑form expression \(t^{*}=2\pi/p\) is correct.
